title: Minimum Flips of k Neighbours

concept.title: The leftmost zero decides
body: You may flip `k` neighbouring bits at a time (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0) and want every bit to be 1. Look at the **leftmost zero**. Only a flip that starts exactly there can fix it without disturbing the bits on its left, so you are forced to flip the window starting at that position. Repeating this greedy rule gives the minimum number of flips (or shows that it is impossible near the right end).

Flipping the window physically costs O(k) each time. To make it fast, remember only **how many active flips cover the current position**: a flip that started at `i` covers `i .. i + k - 1`. The current bit value is `a[i]` changed by the parity of the active flips. Mark the end of a flip in a helper array.

body.code:
flip = 0                       # parity of the flips covering position i
for i in range(n):
    flip ^= end[i]             # a flip that stopped just before i
    if a[i] ^ flip == 0:        # the bit is a 0 now
        if i + k > n: impossible
        flip ^= 1; end[i + k] ^= 1; count += 1

statement: You are given a binary array of length `n` and a number `k`. In one move you choose `k` consecutive positions and flip all their bits (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0). Find the smallest number of moves that makes all the bits 1, or print -1 if it is impossible.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, each 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Print the minimum number of moves, or -1.

examples.note: Flip positions 1-2 to get 1 0 0 1 1, then positions 2-3: 1 1 1 1 1. Two moves.
It is impossible to fix all three bits.

hints: The leftmost 0 can only be fixed by a flip that starts at it.
Keep the parity of the number of flips that cover the current position instead of flipping k bits each time.
If a flip would stick out of the array, the answer is -1.

explanation: The leftmost zero forces a flip starting there. A helper array marks where each flip stops, so the parity of the flips covering a position is maintained in O(1).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

end = [0] * (n + 1)
flip = 0
count = 0
possible = True
for i in range(n):
    flip ^= end[i]
    if a[i] ^ flip == 0:
        if i + k > n:
            possible = False
            break
        flip ^= 1
        end[i + k] ^= 1
        count += 1
print(count if possible else -1)
